key_insight: Airfoil2Vec shows that spectral, geometry-aware encodings can condition neural surrogates to predict airfoil pressure and velocity fields accurately and much faster than CFD.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid aerodynamic evaluation for automotive and motorsport airfoil design, where downforce and flow-field predictions must be explored over many shapes and angles of attack.
method: Built a dataset of ~10,000 steady 2D RANS simulations for downforce-generating NACA 4-digit airfoils.
Compared neural surrogates including neural fields, neural ODEs, MLPs, graph-based models, and spectral geometry-conditioning methods.
Proposed Airfoil2Vec, combining joint contour spectrum with separate camber and thickness spectra to encode airfoil geometry.
evidence_signal: The model was tested on angle-of-attack interpolation, unseen NACA geometries, and non-NACA airfoils, and it preserved aerodynamic quantities and flow structures with orders-of-magnitude speedups over CFD.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the training set covers geometry and operating conditions, so extrapolation to highly novel airfoils or regimes should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Airfoil2Vec: Spectral Geometry-Conditioned Neural Surrogate Models for Airfoil Aerodynamics and a Downforce-Generating CFD Dataset
